narrative.summary: The Gambia has no AI law or national AI strategy yet. Its National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 commits to a first AI Development Policy and Strategy, an AI Ethics Council and a national AI research centre. The Data Protection and Privacy Bill, 2024, shown as assented on the National Assembly tracker, gives people a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, supervised by the Information Commission.

narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026. The enacted text of the data protection law and its Gazette publication could not be found online, so the record follows the National Assembly's bill page. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI guidance from the Central Bank. The planned AI policy and strategy is tracked as a lead.

instruments.current_status: Current national digital economy plan, published on the MoCDE Downloads page; it re-issues, with a 2024-2034 horizon, the 2023-2033 master plan prepared by the e-Governance Academy (dated 14.09.2023). Its section 3.8 flagship 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) Development Policy and Strategy' states that 'there has never been an AI policy and Strategy in The Gambia', and as of October 2026 no national AI policy or strategy was found on official Gambian sites.
instruments.summary: The Gambia's ten-year digital economy master plan, organised in ten pillars (digital infrastructure, digital government, digital financial services, entrepreneurship, innovation ecosystems, skills, cybersecurity and data protection, policy and regulation, cooperation, advocacy). Its flagship projects include an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Development Policy and Strategy (year 2, budget 25,000) to promote AI research, adoption, talent and ethical, responsible-use guidelines; an AI Ethics Council to formulate AI policies, guidelines and best practices protecting privacy and human rights (year 3); and a National Artificial Intelligence Research Center (year 3). It also proposes AI-powered government services such as a virtual assistant for citizen inquiries.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only national government document setting AI policy direction: commits to developing the first national AI policy/strategy and an AI Ethics Council.

instruments.current_status: Status taken from the National Assembly's official bill tracker, which marks the bill 'Assented'. The enacted Act's text and its Gazette publication were not found online, so the assent date, Act number and commencement are unconfirmed.
instruments.summary: General data protection law regulating processing of personal data by automated and non-automated means, with principles of lawful processing, data subject rights, controller and processor duties (transparency, data protection by design, data protection impact assessments covering systematic evaluation based on automated processing including profiling, breach notification), trans-border transfer rules and criminal offences such as re-identification of personal data. Section 12 gives data subjects a right not to be subject to a decision that significantly affects them based solely on automated processing, with exceptions for law, contract or consent subject to safeguards. Oversight is given to the Information Commission established under the Access to Information Act 2021, with powers to investigate and impose penalties and fines.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main binding rule touching AI: automated decision-making and profiling safeguards, DPIAs for automated evaluation.

instruments.current_status: Policy basis for the Data Protection and Privacy Bill, 2024, still listed on the MoCDE Downloads page; page footers read 'Draft Data Protection and Privacy Policy - The Gambia. May 2019' and the cover title is 'Policy and Strategy, 2019'.
instruments.summary: Government policy setting the institutional and legal framework for data protection to give effect to the constitutional right to privacy (section 23). It sets processing principles (fairness, purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, security, accountability), data protection by design, trans-border data flow rules and data subject rights including a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing. It calls for an independent national supervisory authority.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The National Assembly's bill tracker and acts, the digital economy ministry's documents, the government policy repository, ministries and regulators were searched at national level. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for risk and assurance, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, sector rules, generative AI, drafts and consultations, or international agreements.
